newsitem.title: USA: Appeals court rules for Motorola in pager case.
newsitem.headline: Appeals court rules for Motorola in pager case.

text.p: A federal appeals court Thursday threw out an injunction that stopped Motorola Inc. from selling handheld pagers that display updated scores and statistics of the National Basketball Association games as they are played.

The Second Circuit Court of Appeals held that Motorola and Sports Team Analysis and Tracking Systems (STATS) had not unlawfully taken NBA's property by transmitting "real-time" NBA game scores and statistics taken from television and radio broadcasts of games in progress.

The appeals court reversed an injunction issued by a district court judge involving a pager sold by Motorola and marketed under the name "SportsTrax." STATS supplied the game information that is transmitted to the pagers.
The pager became available in January 1996 for about $200.

The order had stopped Motorola and Sports Team Analysis from transmitting NBA sports information via the pagers, STATS' site on America Online's computer dial-up service or other means unless they obtained the NBA's authorisation.
